title: Honest Intervals for Rank-One Matrix Policy Evaluation in Growing Dimension
banked_reason: D0.5.G achieved subfield below field floor: projected paper_score_ceiling 6.8 < 7.4; not salvageable within scope. Math referee PASS and repaired decision review PASS with no findings.
gap_reasons: The proved frontier concerns exact rank one, known Gaussian noise, uniform logging, strong signals proportional to dimension, and d^3/N tending to zero; it does not establish inference for sparse logging or general low-rank policy evaluation.
The transition characteristic function uses population factors, while the feasible interval supplies a conservative probability envelope rather than estimated transition quantiles.

The radius multiplier 2048, restrictive spectral gate, and enormous sufficient onset leave practical usefulness unestablished, and the delivered balanced-sign calculation supplies no coverage or length computations supporting the proposed software application.

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived and independently reviewed a matching ambient-honest interval-length frontier through vanishing tangent alignment, strengthened to arbitrary public even dimensions with d^3/N tending to zero and no explicit incoherence. Mathematical and corrected decision reviews passed, but the narrow experiment, conservative calibration, extreme onset/constants, and absent application validation cap the package at subfield rather than the field floor. Formalization was not started; a field-tier follow-on requires a new research extension rather than a bounded repair.
tldr: For iid Gaussian rank-one policy evaluation, one explicit connected interval has finite-sample coverage at least \(9/10\) on the entire signal-and-entry coverage class and achieves the pointwise optimal expected-length order on its fixed-margin evaluation subset. For every fixed public even sequence \(d_N\ge4\) with \(d_N^3/N\to0\), the frontier is \((d/\sqrt N)\gamma+(d^2/(Ns))\|B\|_{\mathrm F}\). It is uniformly comparable to \((d/\sqrt N)\gamma+N^{-1}\), including exact zero alignment. The constants are universal and the asymptotic onset depends only on the public sequence. Integrated same-sample spectral calibration and finite coupled-factor mixtures in the original iid likelihood prove both sides, while a dependent Gaussian linear--bilinear law describes the single transition.
gap: Ma et al. permit decreasing positive alignment but impose a baseline-dependent projected-norm floor and bound worst-case length. Their inverse-alignment hypotheses exclude zero; their theorem does not establish pointwise expected length under one fixed ambient coverage class with growing unknown factors.
fill: The frontier question joins primitive spectral calibration and original-iid coupled-factor alternatives. The target is one common contrast-indexed ambient-honest interval with uniformly sharp local expected length, including diffuse legal contrasts and the entire vanishing-alignment transition.
